title: Lekhlokhit
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In Nedarim 66b, a man said to his wife: “By a konam vow, you may not benefit from me until you show a beautiful feature of yours to R’ Yishmael son of R’ Yose.” He asked them: “Perhaps her head is beautiful?” They answered: “It is egg-shaped.” He found no part of her beautiful and asked her name. They said: “Lekhlokhit.” He said: “They aptly call her Lekhlokhit, for she is soiled with blemishes.” [The supplied text has ועי״ן. Hyman’s printed text reads “and thereby.”] He released the man from his vow.

notes.text: The fragment ועי״ן before the vow’s release remains unclear. The full Nedarim account confirms the sage as Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yose and plays on Lekhlokhit, “soiled,” and “soiled with blemishes.”

No new primary scalar was returned. The earlier Nedarim account is inherited rather than newly inspected. The conjecture ועי״ז, and thereby, is plausible for supplied ועי״ן but does not prove letter history or settle the fragment; it remains explicit. מום יפה is the paradoxical beautiful blemish, rendered beautiful feature; aptly does not name her Yafa. The wife must show the feature TO the sage within the vow clause. The name pun, plural dialogue replies and negation remain. Egg-shaped is a contextual lexical rendering of סגלגלו; uninspected abbreviated personal titles stay R’.

Hyman’s print (vol. III, p. 864) reads ועי״ז, “and thereby,” where the supplied Hebrew has ועי״ן. His separate article on R’ Yishmael son of R’ Yose (vol. III, p. 837) explains that the sage used the woman’s aptly given name to release the vow. Nedarim 66b gives the full dialogue, including other features omitted in Hyman’s account. The consulted English renders the head “round” and renders the last line as permitting her to benefit from her husband. Hyman’s account describes the release as the man’s release from his vow.
